subject: Post-demo: schema assurance & retry playbook for Veridian pilot
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@veridian.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: schema assurance & retry playbook for Veridian pilot

Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum toward a pilot: 

Summary (what we covered)
- Walked through hosted API + Dedicated options and the SDK quickstart.
- Showed an example embedding -> reranker pipeline and structured output via tool-calling.
- Highlighted runtime features relevant to Veridian: prefix caching, routing by tier/region, and schema enforcement with constrained decoding.

Key asks you flagged
- Strong JSON schema validation on generation output and server-side retries when constrained decoding fails.
- Deep integration with your AWS environment (VPC peering + KMS key handling).
- Predictable latency at 95th percentile during inference-heavy batch reranks.

What we propose (next steps)
1) Technical deep-dive (90 min) with your eng + our infra/serving leads — proposed week of Nov 15.
2) Pilot plan & MAP: 6-week pilot focusing on embedding + reranker throughput and structured-output reliability. Draft included in attached doc ("veridian-ma-mp.docx").
3) Procurement intro: please loop in your procurement contact so we can share pilot SOW and commercials.

Technical pre-read (attached)
- sdk-quickstart-v0.9.patch — small examples for auth patterns and routing snippet
- demo-20271104.mp4 — recording from yesterday
- veridian-ma-mp.docx — mutual action plan draft (pilot milestones + acceptance criteria)

Quick note on the structured-output reliability approach we recommend:
- Constrained decoding at the model layer (format tokens + grammar constraints) to reduce malformed outputs.
- Runtime schema validation: every server-generated payload is validated against a canonical JSON schema; failures are retried with a narrower sampling temperature + alternative model variant if necessary.
- Local SDK validation hooks for early validation and helpful client-side errors to save round trips.

If that looks good, can you confirm:
- A tech deep-dive slot next week (Nov 15–19) that works for your eng lead?
- Procurement contact email for SOW?

Thanks — I’ll schedule the deep-dive tentatively for Nov 16 at 10am PT and send a calendar hold; will cancel if you prefer a different slot.

– Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@veridian.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@veridian.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2027 18:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: schema assurance & retry playbook for Veridian pilot

Markus —

Appreciate the recap and the recording. High level yes, this is what we need. A few clarifications from our side so the pilot scope is accurate: 

1) Schema & retries
- Our legal/QA team requires proof that malformed outputs are detected and either corrected or rejected deterministically; a retry loop is acceptable only when we have a bounded policy (max retries, fallback tokenization).
- We’d like the schema validation to be auditable — logs for each validation failure + reason.

2) Embeddings / Reranker
- We’ll send a 50k document corpus for a performance test. Reranker will be applied to top-100 candidate list from embeddings. We need guidance on batching thresholds to hit 95th p99 latency targets.

3) Security / deployment
- Veridian runs in AWS us-west-2. We require either VPC peering or PrivateLink and customer-managed KMS for keys.

Procurement
- procurement@veridian.ai is on copy — they’ll coordinate SOW and PO once scope is nailed down.

Tech lead for this project is Carlos Rios (c.rios@veridian.ai) — please use him for the deep-dive calendar invite.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Director of Product | Veridian AI

(On a separate note: please send the JSON schema example you referenced in the demo so our QA team can pre-review.)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@veridian.ai>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 06 Nov 2027 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: schema assurance & retry playbook for Veridian pilot

Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks — below are concrete engineering approaches we recommend for the pilot. I’ve tried to keep this actionable so Carlos and your eng team can validate quickly.

1) Constrained decoding + validation flow (server-side)\- Run constrained decoding when we have strict structural requirements (e.g., tool-calls / typed JSON). We use a combination of token-level constraints (prefix enforcement) and post-decode parse checks.
- If parse fails or schema validation fails, server will: 
  a) log failure with a standard code (EX_SCHEMA_PARSE / EX_SCHEMA_VALIDATION) to the request trace,
  b) automatically retry once with: temperature=0.0 and model_variant=stable-1-small,
  c) if retry fails, promote to fallback: return a structured error object (with error_code + canonical_reason) to the SDK so client can decide to re-request or surface to user.

2) SDK + client-side hooks\- We'll include a validation helper in the SDK (node/python) that runs the canonical JSON schema against responses and surfaces structured exceptions. This reduces unnecessary server round trips for obviously invalid client-side inputs.

3) Routing and batching guidance
- For reranker pipelines: continuous batching with a 50–200ms collection window for top-k scoring, and a separate high-priority lane for interactive hits (p95 latency sensitive).
- We'll provide a recommended batching profile based on your 50k corpus after an initial perf sweep.

4) Authentication and key management
- Support for short-lived OIDC tokens + customer HSM/KMS wrapping. For pilot: we can use a customer-managed KMS envelope (you control DEKs) and Redwood manages short-lived tokens via OIDC.

5) Observability / auditing
- All schema validation failures and retry attempts are traced with request_id and persisted in our audit logs (retention per SOW). We can produce an export CSV for your QA audit.

Attachments / examples I’m sending:
- Attached: example-schema.json (snippet included below)

Example: minimal schema we recommend for the reranker response (snippet)
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "candidates": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "object", "properties": { "id": {"type": "string"}, "score": {"type": "number"}, "metadata": {"type": "object"} }, "required": ["id", "score"] } },
    "model_version": {"type": "string"}
  },
  "required": ["candidates", "model_version"]
}

I’ll bring a more detailed playbook (including exact sample code for the retry handler and our tracing keys) to the deep-dive.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: example-schema.json (text))
